subject: May performance spike — usage impact & renewal discussion
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@blueriver.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Sana Iqbal <sana.iqbal@blueriver.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: May performance spike — invoice/usage review requested

Hi Olga,

Quick note from our SRE/ML infra team: during a window on 24–25 May we saw a sustained latency regression on the gpt-lite variant we had pinned for staging->prod traffic. That caused a number of client-side retries and a ~28% increase in token consumption for the affected workloads.

We saw the cost impact on our April–May bill and need a short reconciliation: can you provide the usage breakdown for our account for the 24–26 May window and any analysis you have on root cause? We’ve opened ticket #98721 but wanted to loop you directly.

Separately, our renewal for July is approaching — given the spike and the tight contract we have, we’d like to discuss possible burst credits or a short-term uplift to dedicated capacity to avoid recurrence. Can we schedule a 30-min sync this week?

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Platform, BlueRiver Analytics
ethan.cole@blueriver.ai

Attachments: none
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@blueriver.ai>
Cc: Sana Iqbal <sana.iqbal@blueriver.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: May performance spike — invoice/usage review requested

Ethan — thanks for the heads-up and sorry for the disruption. We investigated with infra and the short summary:

- Root cause: an autoscaling and routing mismatch caused a subset of requests to fall back from your pinned gpt-lite-xq to gpt-base-std while the optimized kernels were rebalanced. The fallback increased per-token latency and triggered a small number of client retries.
- Measured impact: for 2026-05-24 02:00–2026-05-25 18:00 UTC we estimate ~26–30% additional token spend on the affected endpoints (attached: may-usage-summary-blueriver.csv).
- Remediation: runtime fix deployed 05-26 03:20 UTC to tighten routing and avoid fallback cascade; longer-term we recommend a dedicated lane for your prod traffic if you want predictable latency at scale.

We’ve attached a concise log extract (engine-latency-sample-05-24.log) and the usage CSV. I’ll put these into the support ticket #98721 and link the dashboard.

Commercially — to address the bill delta and keep the renewal on track, I propose the following options for your team to consider before our July renewal: 
1) One-time credit covering 75% of the estimated excess token spend for the window above (we’ll reconcile after final logs).
2) 90-day burst credits (200k tokens) + elevated support during the next month while you evaluate Dedicated lanes.
3) Accelerated renewal with a 12-month committed tier at a reduced unit price (we can provide an uplift estimate if you share expected Q3 token trajectory).

If it helps, Ben can draft a short amendment that encodes option 2 and the burst credits while we finalize a multi-month commitment. Do you have a preference? I’m available for a sync Thursday morning PST.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

Attachments: may-usage-summary-blueriver.csv, engine-latency-sample-05-24.log
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@blueriver.ai>, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: May performance spike — invoice/usage review requested

Ethan — jumping in with the commercial path so we can move quickly. Thanks for raising this and thanks Olga for the analysis. Proposed amendment attached. TL;DR commercial options we can do immediately: 

- Option A (short-term relief): Apply a credit equal to 75% of the excess token cost for 24–25 May + 200k burst tokens available thru 2026-08-31. No change to committed term.
- Option B (accelerate and save): Move to a 12-month committed plan starting 2026-07-01 with a 10% unit-price discount and 100k upfront burst tokens. This reduces unit economics going forward and gives you predictable runway.

Operational guarantees: with Option B we can commit to a dedicated serving lane and a P1 on-call path during the first 60 days of the term. We’ve summarized expected ROI in the attached PDF (proposed-amendment-BlueRiver-2026.pdf) — sample math included using your May baseline plus a conservative 2x growth scenario.

Next steps: if you’re good with Option A we can apply the credit to the May invoice and post the burst tokens within 48 hours. If you want Option B, Ben or Marissa can run final numbers and I’ll route the amendment for signature.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed-amendment-BlueRiver-2026.pdf
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@blueriver.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Sana Iqbal <sana.iqbal@blueriver.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: May performance spike — invoice/usage review requested

Thanks — appreciate the quick analysis and the options. We’ll take Option A to get immediate relief and the 200k burst tokens while we evaluate Dedicated lanes. Please apply the credit against May and post the burst tokens; we’ll schedule the Thursday sync you suggested to walk the Dedicated lane requirements (Sana will bring the infra requirements).

Assuming the burst tokens are posted within 48 hours and credit applied, we’ll proceed with a Q3 evaluation and aim to decide on Option B (12-month commit) prior to the July renewal.

Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Platform, BlueRiver Analytics
ethan.cole@blueriver.ai
